what_it_does: Modern chips do not behave identically in every unit — tiny manufacturing variations mean some transistors switch slightly faster or slower than designed (called on-chip variation). Static timing analysis (STA) is the standard tool engineers use to predict whether a chip will run correctly at its target speed; when you include statistical variation, you get Statistical Static Timing Analysis (SSTA), which tracks probability distributions of delay rather than single numbers. SSTA can involve enormous graphs — this paper describes one workload that produces an 18-gigabyte graph — making it slow and memory-hungry. The paper proposes a GPU-based scheduling algorithm that processes this giant timing graph faster by exploiting the GPU's massively parallel architecture, along with a memory management strategy that keeps the computation within the GPU's limited on-board memory. Details of the speedup are not available from the abstract.
